"The front-counter team and floor markings, minutes"
It started on time, and the training lead led the discussion with a calm and careful tone. I regret that several points had to be repeated for clarity, yet the team remained attentive and respectful throughout.

The attendees were Liam Moretti, Mina Hernandez, and Winston, and I recorded their presence as part of the Companion Animal Travel Desk review for Aurelia Skyways. The opening remarks stressed that passengers must receive clear guidance before departure, and that the passenger coordinator should explain the required travel steps in plain language. This was received well, although I apologized for the earlier confusion at the counter and noted that the corrected process must be followed consistently.

The discussion then turned to kennel placement, label checks, and the need to keep the pet area orderly so that animals are moved without delay or distress. <<FACT F047>> The team agreed that the floor markings should continue to guide passengers and staff more clearly, and that any misplaced equipment should be returned at once. I also asked that concerns be raised early so they can be addressed before boarding begins.

A further point concerned the pet cabin and the importance of checking eligibility before acceptance. <<FACT F034>> The group accepted that the handover procedure must remain steady and courteous, and that all records should be completed before the passenger leaves the desk. I apologized again for the extra reminders, but the team understood that accuracy is essential when animals travel.

No other matters were raised, and the meeting concluded with agreement to keep the revised guidance visible at the front counter and to report any future issues promptly.
